app.name: Xero Developer Platform (your own OAuth 2.0 app)

verdict.summary: Creating and connecting your own Xero app takes minutes and needs no review, but Starter tier caps you at five connections. Reaching more customers means paid tiers, and Plus, Advanced and Enterprise apps must go through certification, which needs beta customers, a security assessment and a timeline Xero does not publish.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to create the app and connect your own account; days to weeks of work to get Custom Connections or certification ready
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min once you have a Xero login with the Connected Apps permission
verdict.approval_wait: None for Gate 1 and Starter tier. Certification timeline is not published; Xero says it will share requirements only after you apply.

gates.name: Own account, Starter tier
gates.unlocks: Your app works against your own Xero organisation and Demo Company. You can connect your own user account and test the full OAuth flow.
limits: New apps default to the Starter tier, which caps connections at 5.
Rate limits are 5 concurrent calls and 60 calls per minute per tenant, and 1,000 calls per day on Starter.
The connecting user must have Standard, Adviser or Administrator access with the Connected Apps permission.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after you have a Xero login with the right permission

gates.name: Invited organisations (Custom Connections or uncertified apps)
gates.unlocks: A limited set of other organisations can connect. A Custom Connection is for one organisation at a time, and needs client credentials and a paid Custom Connection subscription. Uncertified apps can connect to other organisations within a cap.
limits: Custom Connections are for one organisation each and are offered only for Australia, New Zealand, the UK and the US.
Custom Connections cannot access the Remote MCP Server.
Uncertified connection cap conflicts across Xero pages: 2 uncertified apps per org (FAQ) vs 5 connections per org (connection-management page). Verify in the portal.
Starter to a sixth connection requires payment details, and Core is $35 AUD per month excluding tax.
gates.time_to_reach: Set-up time varies. Custom Connections need the organisation to buy a subscription before it can authorise.

gates.name: Certified app (Plus, Advanced, Enterprise, or App Store listing)
gates.unlocks: Public use beyond the Starter and Core caps, with Xero App Store listing where required or chosen.
limits: Apps on Plus, Advanced and Enterprise must be certified.
A Xero App Store listing is required on Enterprise, optional on Plus and Advanced, and not available on Starter or Core.
Certification is annual, and a monthly Platform Fee applies after certification.
Journals endpoint, Practice Manager API and Bulk Connections need a security assessment and sit at Advanced tier or above.
gates.time_to_reach: Not published by Xero. A security assessment takes about 5 working days, then 5-10 working days for Xero to review it. Certification also needs beta testing with 10-25 customers.

steps.title: Create a Xero developer account and accept the terms
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Xero developer account on developer.xero.com, then open My Apps at the app-management page. The page needs JavaScript enabled. Click New app and tick the Xero Developer Platform Terms and Conditions before clicking Create App.

values.label: App name
values.value: Any name that does not include the word 'Xero'

gotchas: App names cannot include the word 'Xero'.
The company or application URL must be https.

steps.title: Add the Composio callback URL as a redirect URI
steps.detail: Open your new app, go to the Configuration page, and add the redirect URI. Xero compares it to the redirect URI Composio sends, so it must match exactly, including scheme, host, path and trailing slash.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Xero requires HTTPS redirect URIs, except localhost.
Wildcards are not supported.
Up to 50 redirect URIs per app.
A mismatch returns an 'Invalid URI' error.

steps.title: Generate and store the client secret
steps.detail: On the app's Configuration page, generate a client secret and copy it immediately. Copy the client ID as well. Store the secret in a password manager, because Xero shows it only once.
gotchas: If you lose the secret, generate a new one and update Composio.

steps.title: Enter the client ID and secret in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create or edit the Xero auth config and paste the client ID and client secret from the Xero app. Confirm the redirect URI in Composio matches the one registered in Xero.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: From the Xero app Configuration page

values.label: Client secret
values.value: From step 3, shown once by Xero

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Set the scope list against granular scopes
steps.detail: Compare the Composio default scope list against Xero's current granular scopes. Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use granular scopes automatically. Start with a minimal set such as openid, profile, email, the accounting scopes you actually call, and offline_access. Remove legacy broad scopes you do not use.

values.label: Minimum example set
values.value: openid, profile, email, accounting.invoices, accounting.settings, offline_access

gotchas: offline_access is required to receive a refresh token.
The Composio default list was not verified against Xero's full scope reference.

steps.title: Connect your own Xero account
steps.detail: Run the Composio connection flow with a Xero user who has Standard, Adviser or Administrator access and the Connected Apps permission. For Payroll endpoints the user must be a Payroll Admin. Use a Demo Company if you want a non-production org.
gotchas: Connecting with a user who lacks the Connected Apps permission fails.
Payroll access requires the Payroll Admin role.

steps.title: Build a separate test app for granular-scope work
steps.detail: Xero recommends a separate test app in the Developer Portal to verify granular-scope code against a Demo Company, so the production app is not affected. Repeat steps 1-5 for the test app with its own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Plan token handling
steps.detail: Build refresh logic for 30-minute access tokens. On each refresh, store the replacement refresh token, because the old one is replaced. Keep a retry path using the old refresh token within the 30-minute grace window if the response is lost. Flag connections unused for 60 days, since they will need reauthorisation.
gotchas: Refresh tokens are issued only with offline_access.
Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days.
The 60-day expiry for rotated tokens is confirmed in a community reply and the FAQ.

steps.title: Choose a Gate 2 path: Custom Connection or uncertified connections
steps.detail: Decide whether one organisation at a time (Custom Connection, needs client credentials and a paid subscription, not in other regions) or several organisations (uncertified apps, subject to a cap) fits your product. Confirm the uncertified cap in the developer portal before relying on it. Custom Connections cannot use the Remote MCP Server.

steps.title: Test fully before connecting a live organisation
steps.detail: Build and test the integration against the Demo Company first. Xero advises that integrations be fully built and tested before connecting to a live organisation. Check error handling for rate limits: 60 calls per minute and 1,000 per day on Starter, with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header.
gotchas: Rate limits are the same for all apps and cannot be increased on request.
Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

steps.title: Move past five connections on Starter (paid)
steps.detail: To add a sixth connection on Starter, add payment details in the developer portal. The app then moves to Core. Core is $35 AUD per month excluding tax, and Plus is $245 AUD per month. Tier changes are requested through the developer portal and the app must meet tier requirements first.
gotchas: Connection caps by tier: Starter 5, Core 50, Plus 1,000, Advanced 10,000, Enterprise no limit.
Tier fees are listed in AUD, excluding tax.

steps.title: Prepare the certification file (beta customers, security assessment, Sign Up with Xero)
steps.detail: Recruit 10-25 beta customers, since Xero requires beta testing with at least 10 and up to 25. Implement and maintain Sign up with Xero for all users of the app. Publish a privacy notice and terms of use. Complete the security assessment for premium features or high-volume use, which Xero says takes about 5 working days, followed by 5-10 working days for Xero to assess.
gotchas: Detailed certification requirements are shared only after you apply.
The security assessment is annual as well as initial.
Journals endpoint, Practice Manager API and Bulk Connections need Advanced tier or above.

steps.title: Apply for certification and, if needed, App Store listing
steps.detail: Apply for certification through Xero's partner process. Certification covers connection, branding and naming, app launcher, scopes, error handling, data integrity, account and payment mapping, and taxes. Choose whether to list on the Xero App Store. Listing is required on Enterprise, optional on Plus and Advanced, and not available on Starter or Core.
gotchas: Use case approval criteria are not published; contact Xero support.
Certification is required for Plus, Advanced and Enterprise.

steps.title: Wait for Xero's certification decision
steps.detail: Xero has not published certification review timelines or rejection reasons. Track your application through Xero support and plan for an open-ended wait.
gotchas: No documented minimum-install threshold for a listing was found.

steps.title: Budget for ongoing certified-app fees
steps.detail: Once certified, a monthly Platform Fee applies based on connection tier and premium features. Remove ended connections promptly, because they still count toward the fee until removed. Certification is renewed annually.

requirements.item: Accept the Xero Developer Platform Terms and Conditions
requirements.detail: Required in the New app form before Create App.
Localhost is an exception for redirect URIs only.
The Composio callback URL must be registered exactly. No wildcards. Max 50 per app.
Standard, Adviser or Administrator with Connected Apps. Payroll Admin for Payroll APIs.
Without it, no refresh token is issued.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token.
Five connections. Sixth needs payment details.
One organisation per Custom Connection, in AU, NZ, UK or US, with a purchased subscription.

requirements.item: Privacy notice and terms of use
Sign up with Xero for certified apps
requirements.detail: Must implement and maintain it for all users.
For premium features and certain high-volume consumers. Initial and annual.

requirements.item: Certification for Plus, Advanced and Enterprise
requirements.detail: Required before these tiers are used.

scopes.effect: Needed to receive a refresh token. Without it, you must reauthorise users when the 30-minute access token expires.
Identity scopes in Xero's example authorisation request.
Granular invoice access, from the example set and the Composio default list. Confirm the exact current granular names in the portal.
Organisation settings access, from the example set and the Composio default list.

scopes.scope: Legacy broad accounting scopes in Composio default list
scopes.effect: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use granular scopes, so legacy scopes may be unnecessary or rejected. Check each one before use. Sensitive or restricted classification was not verified.

scopes.scope: projects, files and reporting scopes in Composio default list
scopes.effect: Only request these if your product uses them. Each adds surface for review and user consent.

blockers.symptom: 'Invalid URI' error when Composio starts the authorisation flow
blockers.cause: The redirect URI in the Xero app does not exactly match the one Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Copy the Composio callback URL from the Composio auth config into the Xero app's redirect URIs, character for character.

blockers.symptom: Sixth connection cannot be added to a Starter app
blockers.cause: Starter tier caps connections at five, and a sixth requires payment details.
blockers.fix: Add payment details in the developer portal to move the app to Core, or stay within five connections.

blockers.cause: App names cannot include the word 'Xero'.
The FAQ says two uncertified apps per organisation. The connection-management and Custom Connections pages say five.
blockers.fix: Verify the figure in the developer portal before designing around it.

blockers.cause: Xero shows the client secret only once.
blockers.fix: Generate a new client secret on the Configuration page and update Composio.

blockers.cause: Per-tenant rate limits (5 concurrent, 60 per minute, 1,000 per day on Starter) were exceeded.
blockers.fix: Honour Retry-After, queue calls, and reduce concurrency. Limits cannot be raised on request.

blockers.symptom: Certified-tier apps cannot launch without certification
blockers.cause: Plus, Advanced and Enterprise apps must be certified.
blockers.fix: Plan the beta cohort, security assessment and Sign up with Xero before moving to these tiers.
blockers.contact: Xero support, for use-case approval questions

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Xero, so you must register your own Xero OAuth 2.0 app and paste its client ID and secret into Composio. Add the Composio callback URL to the Xero app's redirect URIs exactly as shown in your Composio auth config. The Composio default scope list is long and mostly legacy broad accounting scopes; check it against the granular scopes before use.

open_questions: Certification review timelines are not published in any source found. Only the security assessment timing and the 10-customer requirement are known.
No official rejection-reason list for certification or App Store listing review was found.
Uncertified connection cap conflicts: FAQ says two per org, connection-management and Custom Connections pages say five. Verify in the developer portal.
The Composio default redirect URI (backend.composio.dev) is in the catalog, but no Composio document confirmed the exact URI. Use the value shown in your Composio auth config.
The full Xero scope reference was not verified. Sensitive or restricted classification of each scope is unknown, so the Composio default list cannot be confirmed as valid.
OpenID Connect discovery location was not confirmed. A probe of the standard login.xero.com discovery path returned not found, though the OAuth overview lists discovery as a topic.
The App Store listing form (logo, demo video, domain verification, privacy URL fields) was not fetched.
Certification checkpoint details and the separate Developer Platform Terms document were not read in full.
Whether Core-tier apps need certification is not stated; findings only say Plus, Advanced and Enterprise must be certified.
Refresh-token expiry (60 days) is confirmed by the FAQ and a community reply; the official token-types page was only partly read.
